events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.44 (model confidence 0.87)
events.body:
This is a route_deviation dispute on a RydeTAXI trip, so meter-based mileage is recoverable where a deviation is not excused. The trip ran Woodlands Civic Centre → Punggol Waterway Point, 19.3 km actual vs 17.3 km optimal, and the meter was charged at $40.18 with distance fare $27.23 over 19.3 km [F1][F2][F6].

One off-route segment exists: 17:41–17:44, 1.76 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.03 km, adding 1.73 km and reaching up to 979 m off the optimal route [F3]. Under RD-1 that segment is an off-route segment subject to the RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 exemptions, and no exemption applies: there is no rider stop request or rider-named place (RD-3), no traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route reported before the detour (RD-4(a)), and no evidence of a driver route proposal accepted by the rider before departure, nor any route chat at all (RD-5) [F3][F7][F8][F12]. The driver's statement claiming an unavoidable accident diversion is only an unsworn statement that adds nothing because the traffic record it relies on shows SELETAR EXPRESSWAY at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h), which is well above band 1–2 and in any event cannot exempt a segment on its own (RD-4(b)) [F9][F10][F11].

The exemption trace also confirms no qualifying RD-4(a) incident [F12], no prior-agreed route change (RD-5), and no rider stop request (RD-3) [F3], so the single 1.73 km segment is a non-exempt detour under RD-1, and RD-2 requires a partial refund of that segment's extra mileage at the trip's per-kilometre rate. Because the fare is metered (RydeTAXI), the per-km rate is distance fare ÷ distance km = $27.23 ÷ 19.3 km = $1.4102/km, and the refund is 1.73 km × $1.4102/km = $2.4397, rounded to $2.44 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

The unmetered excess in the fare beyond the segment sum (the residual gap between the $2.90 excess-distance item and the segment's extra km) is not refunded under RD-2's rule excluding non-segment residuals, and no ERP/toll or unpublished add-on is in the fare, so no FARE-1/FARE-2 adjustment applies [F4][F6][RD-2][FARE-1][FARE-2]. Profiling shows no previous upheld route dispute (0 route disputes upheld in the rider's 90-day record; driver's single upheld dispute is a no-show matter), so RD-6's "repeated" threshold is not met and no account flag is issued [F14][F15][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $2.44 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexcused detour mileage on the 17:41–17:44 off-route segment; no account flag required.

events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your route deviation dispute and found in your favour. The trip had one stretch where the driver left the best route without a valid reason, adding about 1.7 km. No rider stop request, traffic incident or agreed route change excuses it, so you are owed the extra mileage at the trip's per-kilometre meter rate. You will receive a $2.44 Ryde voucher. We're not refunding the rest of the fare difference, since it isn't part of that detour distance. Nothing changes on your account and no flag has been added.

DRIVER: We reviewed the route deviation dispute on this trip and found against you. One stretch of the trip was driven off the best route with no valid excuse: no rider stop request, no reported traffic incident on the replaced stretch, and no route agreed before departure. The extra 1.7 km is therefore being refunded to the rider as a $2.44 Ryde voucher at the trip's per-kilometre meter rate. Your statement about an accident diversion did not change this, since the traffic record for that road showed speeds above the threshold and it does not exempt a segment on its own. No flag is being placed on your account.
